definitions.type: coordinate differentiation and Euclidean notation convention on the given open domain
definitions.definition: On ℝ^n and ℝ^m use the standard Euclidean inner product v·w=∑_k v_k w_k and norm |v|=(v·v)^(1/2). Spatial Lebesgue measure dx is the product of the n ordinary one-dimensional Lebesgue measures in the standard coordinates. For any function on ℝ^n×(0,∞), ∂_{x_j} means its componentwise derivative in spatial coordinate j (1≤j≤n), and ∂_t its componentwise time derivative, where these derivatives exist. In particular u_t=∂_t u, u_tt=∂_t(∂_t u), and ∂_{x_jx_j}u=∂_{x_j}(∂_{x_j}u). For scalar functions the same conventions apply. D_xu denotes the matrix with columns ∂_{x_j}u, and its squared Frobenius norm is ∑_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u|². Smooth means derivatives of every finite order exist and are continuous on the stated open domain. An integral without a displayed measure is the Lebesgue integral; integrable means measurable with finite integral of the absolute value (or norm).

definitions.definition: For every x∈ℝ^n and t>0, Δ_xu(x,t)=∑_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t), component by component.
For every x∈ℝ^n and t>0, e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+∑_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|².

After integrability has been established, define E(t)=∫_{ℝ^n} e(x,t) dx for every t>0. Differentiability and E'(t) mean the ordinary two-sided real derivative on this open time interval, equivalently the derivative of any local extension near t.

inputs.statement: u is jointly smooth on the open set ℝ^n×(0,∞).

For all x∈ℝ^n and t>0, u(x,t)·u_t(x,t)=0 and u_t(x,t)·(u_tt(x,t)−Δ_xu(x,t))=0. Any real scalar a satisfying u_tt−Δ_xu=a u at that point equals ∑_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|². The density e is smooth on ℝ^n×(0,∞), the mixed derivatives satisfy ∂_t∂_{x_j}u=∂_{x_j}u_t for every 1≤j≤n, and e_t(x,t)=2u_t(x,t)·u_tt(x,t)+2∑_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_j}u(x,t)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t). In particular this displayed e_t is continuous.

inputs.statement: For every t>0, e(·,t) is integrable. More precisely, for each t0>0 there exist a compact C⊂ℝ^n, R>0 and B≥0 such that, writing J=[t0/2,3t0/2] and Q=[−R,R]^n, one has C⊂(−R,R)^n, u(x,r)=q for x∉C and r∈J, and all positive-order derivatives of u vanish for x∉C and r∈int J. The box Q has Lebesgue measure (2R)^n<∞. For every r∈int J, each of the spatial functions e, e_t, u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, u_t·∂_{x_j}u, and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), evaluated at time r, is continuous, vanishes outside C, and is integrable on ℝ^n, for each 1≤j≤n. Finally |e_t(x,r)|≤B for all (x,r)∈Q×[3t0/4,5t0/4].

Let A be a measurable space with a measure μ, and G a normed additive commutative group and real normed vector space. Let I be an index type and l a countably generated filter on I. Given F:I→A→G, f:A→G and b:A→ℝ, assume (i) eventually in l, F(i) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable; (ii) eventually in l, |F(i,x)|≤b(x) for μ-a.e. x; (iii) b is μ-integrable; (iv) for μ-a.e. x, F(i,x) tends along l to f(x). Then ∫ F(i,x) dμ tends along l to ∫ f(x) dμ.

locals.declaration: Choose C from N002 at t0.
Choose R together with C and B from N002 at t0.
Choose B together with C,R from N002 at t0.
Define bnd(x)=B 1_Q(x), the function equal to B on Q and zero elsewhere.
For 0<|h|<η define F(h,x)=(e(x,t0+h)−e(x,t0))/h; at other h set F(h,x)=0. Only the punctured germ at zero is used.

argument.text: Fix t0>0 and choose the compatible witnesses C,R,B from N002. Set Q=[−R,R]^n and η=t0/4. Then [t0−η,t0+η]=[3t0/4,5t0/4]⊂(t0/2,3t0/2). N002 proves |e_t|≤B on the corresponding space-time box. N001 gives that r↦e(x,r) is differentiable at each point of this interval with derivative e_t(x,r). For every x∈Q and 0<|h|<η, apply M004 on this real convex interval with endpoints t0,t0+h. It yields |e(x,t0+h)−e(x,t0)|≤B|h|. Outside Q both densities are zero by N002, since C⊂int Q. Therefore the absolute difference quotient is ≤B1_Q(x) for every x∈ℝ^n.

produces.statement: For all real h with 0<|h|<η and all x∈ℝ^n, |(e(x,t0+h)−e(x,t0))/h|≤B1_Q(x).

argument.text: Define bnd(x)=B1_Q(x). Q is closed and has finite measure (2R)^n by N002. M009 with constant B and set Q gives integrability of B on Q. Extending this restricted constant by zero off the measurable Q is exactly bnd, so bnd is integrable on ℝ^n.

produces.statement: bnd(x)=B1_Q(x) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n.

argument.text: Define F(h,x) as the difference quotient for 0<|h|<η and zero otherwise. For these small nonzero h, its spatial section is continuous by N001 and is integrable by N002 and linearity of integrability. Hence it is a.e. strongly measurable. At every fixed x the difference quotients tend, as h→0 through h≠0, to e_t(x,t0), by N001. F001 and F002 give an integrable bound for the punctured germ. Apply M001 to Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n, scalar codomain ℝ, parameter h∈ℝ with filter 𝓝[≠]0, F as just defined, f(x)=e_t(x,t0), and bound bnd. The filter is countably generated, with the punctured intervals 0<|h|<1/k for positive integers k as a countable neighborhood basis. Consequently ∫F(h,x)dx→∫e_t(x,t0)dx along that filter.

produces.statement: As h→0 with h≠0, ∫_{ℝ^n} F(h,x) dx tends to ∫_{ℝ^n} e_t(x,t0) dx.

argument.text: N002 discharges the guard for E and gives integrability of e(·,t0+h) and e(·,t0) at the nearby positive times, as well as of e_t(·,t0). For 0<|h|<η, linearity of the integral gives ∫F(h,x)dx=(E(t0+h)−E(t0))/h. F003 is therefore exactly the difference-quotient criterion for differentiability of this finite real-valued E: E'(t0)=∫e_t(x,t0)dx. Substitute the full e_t identity from N001. Every summand is integrable by N002. H002 ensures the derivative notation has its usual classical meaning on the open time-domain. Since t0 was arbitrary, this proves the full differentiation assertion.
